statements.status_notes: sqlparse contains a regular expression vulnerable to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service), introduced in commit e75e358. Parsing a crafted SQL string makes the parser spend exponential time in the regular expression, so the calling process hangs. Fixed in sqlparse 0.4.4 by commit c457abd5f.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in sqlparse 0.4.4. Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 through 5.0.2 ship sqlparse 0.4.3 inside the GraalPy virtual environment of the checks extension; 5.0.3 and later ship 0.5.3, and 6.0.0 ships 0.6.0, all outside the range. sqlparse is not run by any check Liquibase bundles, but the helper module liquibase_utilities.py shipped in 5.0.0 through 5.1.1 imports it and exposes split_statements() (sqlparse.split) and tokenize() (sqlparse.parse) to customer-authored Python checks; from 5.2.0 the helper no longer imports sqlparse. The vulnerable regular expression is therefore reachable only when a customer has written and configured a custom Python check that calls those helpers, or imports sqlparse itself, on changelog SQL. The SQL it parses is the changelog the operator is deploying, so an attacker would need to author a changeset in that changelog, which already grants them DDL on the target; the impact of the ReDoS is a hung checks run on the operator's own host.

sqlparse ReDoS vulnerability. sqlparse is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its SQL parsing functionality is never invoked at runtime. Liquibase uses its own Java SQL parser; the Python sqlparse module is never called.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse: TokenList.__init__ materializes O(subtree) value per group, causing CPU denial of service before depth and token caps trigger. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, SQL_REGEX in sqlparse/keywords.py and the per-position loop in sqlparse/lexer.py repeatedly scan unmatched dollar-quoted literal and multiline-comment delimiters, causing quadratic CPU consumption through sqlparse.parse(), sqlparse.format(), and sqlparse.split(). This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse/filters/output.py fails to escape existing backslashes before quotes in sqlparse.format output_format='python' and output_format='php' and the corresponding sqlformat -l modes, allowing crafted SQL to terminate the generated string and inject Python or PHP code when a downstream consumer executes or imports the generated source. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable Python/PHP output-formatting code path (sqlparse.format with output_format='python' or 'php') is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in one of those modes; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) and sqlformat --reindent route attacker-controlled parenthesized tuple lists through ReindentFilter._get_offset() in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, where _flatten_up_to_token() repeatedly rebuilds and joins the statement prefix. Thousands of offset calculations walk an expanding token tree, producing quadratic CPU consumption for inputs that remain below MAX_GROUPING_TOKENS and causing request delays, reduced throughput, or worker starvation. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable reindent code path (sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) or sqlformat --reindent) is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in that mode against attacker-influenced SQL; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse: formatting a list of tuples leads to denial of service. Formatting a long list of tuples with sqlparse hangs, causing excessive CPU consumption. Fixed in 0.5.4.
